briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 15, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Policy Reversals and the Spread of Climate Change Denial
sections.content: Former U.S. President Donald Trump has sparked significant international concern by labeling the risks of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a 'hoax,' similar to climate change [1]. Despite growing global concerns over climate change-related phenomena such as floods in Nepal, the United States is moving to repeal regulations curbing greenhouse gas emissions from power plants [2, 10, 60, 67, 68, 69, 73, 76, 82, 89]. This move is seen as a rollback of key climate change regulations from the Biden administration era, interpreted as an attempt to prevent future presidents from combating climate change [57, 85]. Furthermore, a bill has passed in Florida to remove the term 'climate change' from state statutes, and reports indicate a decrease in mentions of the climate crisis by Democratic politicians since Trump's election in 2024 [92]. Such policy reversals eliminate crucial tools for addressing the climate crisis, risking an acceleration of global warming [67, 82].

sections.title: ⚠️ The Severe Reality of Climate Change: Widespread Domestic and International Damage
sections.content: This year's heatwaves are considered a precursor to climate change, with 95.3% of domestic horticultural farms reporting severe damage due to abnormal high temperatures and heatwaves [4, 5, 8, 9]. After the summer, numerous potholes have appeared nationwide, indicating that climate change is impacting road infrastructure and highlighting the urgent need for climate-responsive road policies [11, 12]. Internationally, global warming is already projected to breach the 1.5-degree limit, with record-breaking ocean heat emphasizing the intensifying impacts of climate change [56, 75]. The floods in Nepal and the tragic case of Joseon in 1670 serve as warnings that the climate crisis first devastates the most vulnerable areas. Climate change threatens human lives in various forms, including the spread of diseases and pests that endanger crops and forests, severe impacts on U.S. water systems, and extreme heat, wildfires, hurricanes, and floods that prevent children from attending school [16, 58, 61, 63, 64, 65, 74]. Scientists warn that overlooked climate feedbacks could worsen global warming by an additional 30% by 2100, and economic impacts are growing, with droughts affecting prices [15, 79].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts and Achievements for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Several local governments in Korea are excelling in implementing carbon neutrality. Gunpo City, by installing a solar power plant in a soundproof tunnel and transforming space limitations into carbon neutrality potential, was awarded the Minister's Award from the Ministry of Climate, Energy, and Environment for '2026 Local Government Carbon Neutrality Best Practices,' ranking second nationwide [17, 18, 20, 22, 26, 27, 30, 31]. Gwanak-gu also received a ministerial award for its carbon neutrality efforts through resident proposals and daily practices, while Dongjak-gu, Namseoul University, and Susin Elementary School are actively operating carbon neutrality education programs that encompass all generations [19, 23, 25, 29, 32]. In the corporate sector, DL Group has published its sustainability management report, expanded ESG education for partners, and analyzed climate risks, disclosing its ESG strategies and achievements [13, 14]. Hwaseong City Research Institute has quantified the carbon reduction effects of items from recycling centers, and Chungnam highway rest areas are also participating in 'Chungnam-type Carbon Neutrality,' demonstrating comprehensive efforts [24, 28].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition: Technological Innovation and Policy Support
sections.content: Amidst positive evaluations of Korea's renewable energy projects and the expressed commitment to expand project scale to 1GW, LS Electric and KEPCO have jointly developed 'grid-forming,' a next-generation grid technology for stabilizing the distribution network during increased renewable energy generation, tackling a significant challenge [34, 35, 41]. Jeju Island has embarked on designing an 'AI Great Transformation' based on renewable energy, and Google DeepMind has unveiled 'WeatherNext 3,' an AI weather model targeting wind and solar grid operators, accelerating the integration of renewable energy and AI [36, 37, 55]. The expansion of data centers in India is highlighting the need for 24/7 clean power, transforming the renewable energy paradigm, while China, entering an era of 60% renewable energy, is focusing on 'connecting well' rather than 'more' [38, 49]. The government has launched the 'Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Committee' to rebuild the solar supply chain, and Jeonbuk Self-Governing Province is actively boosting policy support, including on-site inspections of renewable energy grid saturation and promoting the 'Sunshine and Wind Pension' initiative [52, 53]. Furthermore, renewable energy has saved 4.4 trillion won over five months, acting as an 'economic breakwater' against energy crises, and ESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) are being emphasized as crucial vessels for storing renewable energy [47, 54].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Call for Climate Action and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Prince William, the Prince of Wales, emphasized that gradual actions cannot solve climate change and urged urgent measures, with his optimism regarding climate change being received as an important message [83, 84, 88]. The ASEAN region is disproportionately affected by climate change but is simultaneously seeking new opportunities [87]. It has been argued that Ulsan's climate response strategy should shift towards resilience, and Yongin City plans to establish its 2027 climate response policies by reflecting the opinions of horticultural farmers [3, 7]. Countries worldwide are strengthening infrastructure adaptation efforts, such as actively adopting PC panel paving to respond to climate change [6]. Meanwhile, the UK is experiencing the 'paradox of the nuclear power vacuum,' with gas consumption increasing despite renewable energy accounting for 52.5% of electricity generation. Europe, recognizing that renewable energy alone cannot suffice, is taking a bold step with '50GW of nuclear power,' facing complex challenges in the energy transition process [33, 45].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the severe reality of the climate crisis, alongside the diverse efforts being made both domestically and internationally to overcome it. Amidst warnings against policy reversals, the urgent need for active carbon neutrality practices and accelerated renewable energy transition becomes even more critical. This concludes the daily climate briefing for September 15, 2026.
